# Plan: cache profile summaries in one process

## Measured problem and accepted scope
The existing profile-summary service has one active process. A one-week trace
shows repeated reads of about 900 hot keys: DB CPU is 70%, with read p95 120 ms.
Add a process-local LRU wrapper to the existing repository. Acceptance targets
are at least 60% cache hits, DB CPU below 50%, and read p95 below 60 ms, with the
existing error-rate and correctness SLOs unchanged. This is an internal backend
change with no UI, API, schema, pricing, or developer onboarding change.

## Existing contracts retained
- All reads and writes use this repository in the same process; there are no
  external DB writers. Multi-process operation remains unsupported and startup
  rejects that configuration while caching is enabled.
- Authentication and authorization run before repository access. Keys encode
  the authenticated tenant ID and validated profile ID without ambiguity.
  Values are immutable profile-summary DTOs; secrets and cache keys are never
  logged. Cached results cannot bypass authorization.
- The existing LRU adapter supports 1000 entries, a 16 MiB byte cap, and a
  30-second TTL. Recorded hot data fits those limits. Absent records use a
  distinct sentinel with a 10-second TTL; undefined means a cache miss.
- Cache operations are synchronous and atomic in the single JS event loop.
  On any cache failure the existing adapter bypasses the cache until an empty
  cache is reinitialized; repository errors keep the current typed API error
  mapping. The existing per-key
  single-flight wrapper coalesces simultaneous misses and releases on failure.
- A read already in progress when a write commits may return its earlier DB
  snapshot to that caller. Every read begun after that write completes must
  observe the committed version. TTL expiry is not a substitute for this rule.
  ("Completes" = `writeProfile` returns to its caller. This is the invariant
  every finding below is measured against.)

## Proposed wrapper integration
Keep the current read-through repository interface and shared adapters. These
are the complete new read/write ordering rules; no additional version checks or
coordination between a cache fill and a write are proposed
*(superseded by amendment D1 below; original sketch kept for the record)*:

```javascript
async function readProfile(key) {
  const cached = cache.get(key);
  if (cached !== undefined) return cached;
  const value = await repository.read(key);
  cache.set(key, value);
  return value;
}

async function writeProfile(key, update) {
  const saved = await repository.write(key, update);
  cache.delete(key);
  return saved;
}
```

## Verification and rollout
Existing repository contract tests cover tenant isolation, key validation,
absence, DB failures, and authorization. New wrapper tests cover hit/miss,
eviction and byte limits, TTL, adapter-failure fallback, successful-write
invalidation, failed-write preservation *(superseded by D2: failed-write
invalidation)*, and concurrent-miss coalescing.
The rollout uses the existing runtime feature flag: enable for 10% of keys,
then 50%, then all keys after one healthy hour at each stage. Monitor hit/miss,
eviction, cache bytes, fallback errors, DB CPU, and read p95 without raw IDs.
On error-rate or latency regression, disable the flag immediately; both reads
and writes bypass the cache while disabled *(amended by D6: reads consult the
flag, writes always invalidate while a cache instance exists)*, and enabling
creates an empty cache.
Cold starts remain within the existing DB capacity. The service owner monitors
the rollout and records the results against the acceptance targets.

## Out of scope
Distributed caching, cross-process coherence, prewarming, changing consistency
semantics, or adding new product surfaces. The repository interface preserves a
future replacement path without introducing a general cache framework now.

---

## Accepted plan amendments (CEO review, HOLD SCOPE, 2026-09-09)

Scope is unchanged. Every amendment repairs a gap between the sketch and a
stated invariant or acceptance target. Decision IDs (D0–D7) are defined in the
Decision Record below; this section is the resulting plan text.

### Amended wrapper (replaces the sketch above)

```javascript
// Ordering rule: a write invalidates the cache entry AND any in-flight fetch
// for the key, on every outcome, regardless of per-key flag state. A fetch
// only fills the cache if no write invalidated it while it was in flight.
//
//   R1 miss ──▶ DB read (v1) ─────────────────────▶ resume: flight.invalidated? skip fill
//   W        ──▶ DB write (v2) ──▶ finally: cache.delete + inflight.invalidate
//   R2 (after W returns) ──▶ miss ──▶ fresh flight ──▶ v2   ✓

async function readProfile(key) {
  if (!flag.readsEnabledFor(key)) return repository.read(key);   // D6: flag lookup failure ⇒ false
  const cached = cache.get(key);          // D3: null = cached ABSENT; undefined = miss
  if (cached !== undefined) return cached;
  const flight = inflight.getOrStart(key, () => repository.read(key));
  const value = await flight.promise;     // typed repository errors propagate unchanged
  if (!flight.invalidated) cache.set(key, value);   // D1 guard; D3: null ⇒ ABSENT sentinel, 10 s TTL
  return value;
}

async function writeProfile(key, update) {
  try {
    return await repository.write(key, update);
  } finally {
    cache.delete(key);                    // D2: on success AND failure
    inflight.invalidate(key);             // D1: mark current flight stale, detach it
  }
}
```

Single-flight contract additions (D1): `invalidate(key)` sets
`flight.invalidated = true` and removes it from the map so the next miss starts
a fresh fetch; settle-time release removes the map entry only if it still
points at the same flight object. No unbounded per-key state: the marker lives
on the existing in-flight entry.

### Amended contracts
- **D2** Write failure of any class (validation, conflict, timeout, connection
  reset) invalidates the key. Cost: one extra DB read after a failed write.
  Test "failed-write preservation" becomes "failed-write invalidation".
- **D3** `repository.read` returns `null` for an absent record, never
  `undefined`. `cache.set(key, null)` stores the ABSENT sentinel with the 10 s
  TTL; `cache.get` translates the sentinel back to `null`. `undefined` remains
  the only miss signal. Absent-then-create is covered by the write invalidation.
- **D4** Adapter behavior is classified: an oversized value (> byte cap) or a
  full cache is a *skip* (`set` is a no-op, counter increments, cache stays
  ACTIVE). Only a thrown adapter error (corrupt internal state, size accounting
  failure) flips the adapter to BYPASSED. Adapter methods never throw to the
  wrapper. BYPASSED persists until the flag is toggled off then on.
- **D5** Observability is a deliverable: metrics `profile_cache_state` (gauge
  0 = disabled, 1 = active, 2 = bypassed), `profile_cache_hits_total`,
  `_misses_total`, `_evictions_total`, `_bytes`, `_fill_skipped_stale_total`,
  `_set_skipped_oversize_total`, `_fallback_errors_total`, plus existing DB CPU
  and read p95. One structured log line on ACTIVE→BYPASSED with error class,
  flag stage, and entry count (no keys). Alerts: state = BYPASSED for 5 min;
  hit ratio < 40% for 15 min at the 100% stage; fallback errors > 0 in 5 min.
  Dashboard panels: hit ratio, state, evictions, bytes, DB CPU, read p95.
  Runbook: BYPASSED → toggle flag off, confirm state 0, toggle on, confirm
  state 1 and hit ratio recovering within 2 min; regression → flag off.
  "Healthy hour" = no alert fired, error rate and p95 within SLO.
- **D6** Flag semantics: per-key selection uses a stable hash of the cache key.
  Only reads consult the flag. Writes always run the `finally` invalidation
  while a cache instance exists. A failed flag lookup evaluates to "reads
  disabled". Fully disabling the flag drops the cache instance; enabling
  creates an empty one.
- **D7** The ordering diagram above ships as a code comment on the wrapper and
  the single-flight `invalidate` method, plus a short section in the
  repository README naming the invariant and the four ordering rules.

### Amended verification
Existing contract tests unchanged. Wrapper tests: hit/miss, eviction and byte
limits, TTL (injected clock, no wall-clock sleeps), adapter-failure bypass,
oversize skip keeps ACTIVE (D4), absent → null cached 10 s then create
invalidates (D3), successful-write invalidation, failed-write invalidation (D2),
concurrent-miss coalescing, and controlled pause/release ordering tests for the
two schedules in Section 4 (D1). Partial-rollout test: key cached at 50%,
dropped to 10%, written, restored to 50% ⇒ next read misses (D6). Metric
assertions: each counter increments on its path (D5).

---

## CEO Review Decision Record

### Step 0 — Premise, leverage, dream state, alternatives, mode
- **Premise (0A):** Real, measured pain (70% DB CPU, p95 120 ms, 900 hot keys
  over one week). Doing nothing leaves DB headroom shrinking. A local
  read-through cache is the most direct path; targets are stated and checkable.
  Not a proxy problem.
- **Existing leverage (0B):** LRU adapter (limits, TTL, sentinel, bypass),
  per-key single-flight, runtime feature flag, typed repository errors,
  repository contract tests. The plan reuses all of them and builds no parallel
  flow. Nothing is rebuilt.
- **Dream state (0C):**
  ```
  CURRENT STATE                THIS PLAN                       12-MONTH IDEAL
  1 process, no cache   --->   local read-through cache   ---> same interface, cache
  DB CPU 70%, p95 120ms        behind the repository,          backend swappable if
                               flag-gated, invariant-safe      multi-process ever lands
  ```
  Moves toward the ideal: the repository interface stays the seam.
- **Alternatives (0C-bis):**
  ```
  APPROACH A: Sketch as written (delete-after-write)      Effort S  Risk Med
    Pros: smallest diff; reuses everything
    Cons: stale fill after concurrent write violates the read-after-write
          invariant (Section 4); no coverage of failed writes or partial rollout
  APPROACH B: Sketch + in-flight invalidation marker      Effort S  Risk Low   (recommended)
    Pros: meets the invariant; state lives on existing single-flight entry;
          ~20 LOC delta; fully testable with pause/release
    Cons: single-flight contract grows one method; one more test family
  APPROACH C: Versioned rows + compare-on-fill             Effort L  Risk Med
    Pros: general coherence primitive
    Cons: needs a schema version column, which the accepted scope excludes
  ```
  **D0 (auto-accepted, recommended): Approach B.** Completeness A=5/10,
  B=10/10, C=10/10 but out of scope. Mapped to "handle more edge cases" and
  "right-sized diff".
- **Mode (0F):** HOLD SCOPE, preselected by the user. No expansions surfaced.
- **HOLD analysis (0D):** Touches ~4 files (wrapper, single-flight, adapter
  contract, tests) plus metrics/alert config. No complexity smell. Minimum set
  = the amended wrapper; every amendment is required by a stated invariant or
  target, none is deferrable.
- **Temporal interrogation (0E):** Implementation decisions resolved now:
  invalidation across in-flight fetches (D1), write-failure semantics (D2),
  absent representation (D3), adapter failure vs skip (D4), alert thresholds
  and "healthy" definition (D5), flag semantics and hash (D6), where the
  ordering rules are documented (D7). Effort: human ~1.5 days / CC ~45 min.
- Skipped per run rules: system audit, environment setup, landscape web
  search, brain context, prior learnings, telemetry.

### Findings (each recorded once)

| ID | Section | Evidence (plan text) | Failure mode | Selected remedy | Residual risk | Verification |
|----|---------|----------------------|--------------|-----------------|---------------|--------------|
| D1 | 1, 4 | "no additional version checks or coordination between a cache fill and a write"; invariant "every read begun after that write completes must observe the committed version" | Read misses, awaits DB (v1); write commits v2 and returns; read resumes and fills v1; later reads hit stale v1 up to 30 s. Also a post-write miss joins the pre-write in-flight fetch and receives v1 | In-flight invalidation marker; fill only if not invalidated; post-write misses start a fresh fetch. Original reader still returns v1 to its own caller (allowed: it began before commit) | None against the invariant. Extra DB read per invalidated flight, counted | Pause/release tests for both schedules in Section 4; `fill_skipped_stale_total` increments |
| D2 | 2 | Sketch deletes only after a successful write; test "failed-write preservation" | Write times out after the DB committed; cache keeps v1 up to 30 s; caller retry or re-read sees stale data | `finally` invalidation on every write outcome; rename test | One wasted DB read after a failed write | Test: write rejects ⇒ next read misses and hits DB |
| D3 | 5 | "undefined means a cache miss"; sketch `cache.set(key, value)` with unspecified absent value | If `repository.read` returns `undefined` for absent, absents are never cached and every missing-profile read hits the DB; if the sentinel leaks, callers receive an internal object | Pin: absent = `null`; adapter maps null ⇄ sentinel; wrapper passes null through | None | Test: absent read hits DB once, then served null for 10 s; create invalidates |
| D4 | 2 | "On any cache failure the existing adapter bypasses the cache until an empty cache is reinitialized" | One oversized value or a full cache classified as "failure" trips a sticky bypass; hit rate drops to 0 with no read errors | Classify skip vs failure; adapter never throws to wrapper; bypass only on thrown adapter error | Sticky bypass still requires operator toggle (alerted by D5) | Test: oversize set is a no-op, state stays ACTIVE, counter increments; thrown adapter error ⇒ BYPASSED |
| D5 | 8, 9 | "Monitor hit/miss, eviction, cache bytes, fallback errors, DB CPU, and read p95"; no alerts, gauge, runbook, or "healthy" definition | Sticky BYPASSED or hit-ratio collapse is visible only if someone is watching; rollout "healthy hour" is undefined | Named metrics, state gauge, three alerts, dashboard panels, runbook, healthy definition | Alert thresholds may need tuning after first week | Metric assertions in tests; alert rules reviewed before 10% stage |
| D6 | 9, 4 | "both reads and writes bypass the cache while disabled"; "enable for 10% of keys" | Stage 50% → 10% → 50%: keys cached at first 50% stage are not deleted by writes during the 10% stage and revive stale when restored. Flag lookup failure behavior unspecified | Writes always invalidate while a cache instance exists; stable key hash; flag failure ⇒ reads disabled | None against the invariant | Partial-rollout test in Amended verification |
| D7 | 10 | Ordering rules exist only in this plan | New engineer in 12 months cannot see why `invalidate` exists; stale mental model recreates D1 | Code-comment diagram on wrapper and `invalidate`; README section | Diagram maintenance is part of future changes | Reviewer checks comment matches code in PR |

### Section outcomes (11 of 11 evaluated)
1. **Architecture:** 1 finding → D1. Diagram in Diagrams §1. Coupling added: wrapper ↔ single-flight `invalidate` (justified, in-process). Single point of failure: the one process, unchanged. 10x load: LRU at 1000 entries thrashes first (watch item, see Section 7). Rollback: flag off, seconds.
2. **Error & rescue map:** 9 error paths mapped (registry below); 2 gaps → D2, D4. No catch-all handlers introduced; `finally` runs cleanup only and rethrows nothing new.
3. **Security & threat model:** No issues found. No new endpoint, input, dependency, or secret. Keys are tenant-scoped after authz, so no cross-tenant hit or existence oracle. Negative cache is within an already-authorized tenant. DTOs in process memory match existing handling. Keys never logged (D5 log line carries none).
4. **Data flow & interaction edge cases:** 2 unhandled orderings → D1 (schedule in Diagrams §2b), 1 rollout ordering → D6. No UI interactions; interaction table not applicable.
5. **Code quality:** 1 finding → D3. Naming, DRY, and structure fit the existing adapter/single-flight patterns. Branch count per function ≤ 3. No over-engineering: the marker reuses existing state.
6. **Test review:** Diagram in Diagrams §7. Gaps are the consequences of D1–D6 (tests listed in Amended verification) plus test hygiene: TTL tests use an injected clock. No new behavioral choice needed. 2 a.m. Friday test: pause/release stale-fill schedule. Hostile QA: write during in-flight read at every stage of the flag. Chaos: force adapter throw mid-traffic and confirm BYPASSED alert and unchanged error rate. Pyramid: many unit, 1 integration (flag + wrapper + repository fake), 0 E2E. Load test: replay the one-week hot-key trace against a staging DB before 10%.
7. **Performance:** No issues found. Cache ops O(1) sync. Memory bounded at 16 MiB. TTL floor ≈ 30 DB reads/s for 900 keys. Watch item (not a TODO, capacity growth is an expansion): 900 hot keys against 1000 entries leaves 10% headroom; if `evictions_total` climbs while hit ratio < 60%, the entry cap is the cause.
8. **Observability:** 1 gap → D5.
9. **Deployment & rollout:** 1 risk → D6; "healthy" definition folded into D5. No migration. Deploy order: code deploy with flag off → 10% → 50% → 100%, one healthy hour each. Diagrams §5, §6.
10. **Long-term trajectory:** Reversibility 5/5 (flag plus small wrapper). Debt: 1 item → D7. Path dependency: none; repository seam preserved for a future backend. 1-year question: answered by D7.
11. **Design & UX:** SKIPPED, justified: plan states no UI, API, or product surface change.

### Outside voice
Skipped. `.gstack-section-state-QPMuNw/config.yaml` sets `codex_reviews: disabled`. Per the documented control, no challenge prompt was built, no outside CLI or Agent fallback was dispatched, and outside coverage is reported as **disabled**. Re-enable: `gstack-config set codex_reviews enabled`. The `outside_status: disabled` review-log record was not persisted: no shell tool is available in this run.

### Required outputs

**NOT in scope** (considered, deferred, with reason)
- Distributed or cross-process cache: excluded by the accepted scope statement.
- Versioned rows / compare-on-fill (Approach C): needs a schema change.
- Prewarming and automatic recovery from BYPASSED: alternatives to adequate accepted remedies (D5 alert + runbook); HOLD SCOPE.
- Raising the 1000-entry cap: hypothetical capacity; watch item only.

**What already exists** — LRU adapter (limits, TTL, sentinel, bypass): reused, contract pinned by D3/D4. Single-flight wrapper: reused, gains `invalidate` (D1). Runtime feature flag: reused, semantics pinned by D6. Typed repository errors and contract tests: reused unchanged.

**Dream state delta** — After this plan the service has a flag-gated, invariant-safe local cache behind the unchanged repository interface. The 12-month ideal (swappable backend if multi-process arrives) remains reachable through the same seam; nothing here forecloses it.

**Error & Rescue Registry**

| Method/codepath | What can go wrong | Error class | Rescued? | Action | User sees |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| readProfile → flag lookup | flag service unavailable | FlagLookupError | Y (D6) | treat as reads disabled, counter | nothing |
| readProfile → cache.get | adapter internal error | AdapterError (internal) | Y (D4) | adapter → BYPASSED, log once, read continues to DB | nothing |
| readProfile → repository.read | record absent | (null result) | Y (D3) | cache ABSENT 10 s, return null | existing not-found |
| readProfile → repository.read | DB timeout / connection error | DbTimeoutError / DbConnectionError | Y (existing) | single-flight releases, no fill, typed API error | existing error mapping |
| readProfile → repository.read | authorization failure | AuthorizationError | Y (existing, before repository) | never reaches cache | existing 403 |
| readProfile → single-flight joiners | leader rejects | same error as leader | Y (existing) | all joiners receive leader's typed error | existing error mapping |
| readProfile → cache.set | value > byte cap / cache full | (skip, no error) | Y (D4) | no-op, `set_skipped_oversize_total` | nothing |
| readProfile → cache.set | adapter internal error | AdapterError (internal) | Y (D4) | → BYPASSED, log once, value still returned | nothing |
| writeProfile → repository.write | validation / conflict / timeout | typed repository errors | Y (existing + D2) | rethrow unchanged; `finally` invalidates | existing error mapping |

**Failure Modes Registry**

| Codepath | Failure mode | Rescued? | Test? | User sees? | Logged? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| read fill vs concurrent write | stale fill after write returned | Y (D1) | Y (pause/release) | fresh data | counter |
| post-write miss joins pre-write flight | stale value to new reader | Y (D1) | Y | fresh data | counter |
| write fails after DB commit | stale entry survives | Y (D2) | Y | fresh data on re-read | typed error log (existing) |
| absent record returns undefined | negative cache never fills | Y (D3) | Y | not-found, one DB read per 10 s | hits/misses |
| sentinel leaks to caller | internal object returned | Y (D3) | Y | null | n/a |
| oversized value | sticky bypass | Y (D4) | Y | nothing | counter |
| adapter throws | sticky bypass, hit rate 0 | Y (D4, D5) | Y | nothing; alert to operator | log line + gauge + alert |
| stage 50→10→50 | stale revival | Y (D6) | Y | fresh data | n/a |
| flag lookup fails | undefined read path | Y (D6) | Y | nothing (DB read) | counter |
| LRU thrash at 10x keys | hit ratio < target | N/A (watch) | load test | slower reads, correct | evictions + alert |

CRITICAL GAPS remaining: 0.

**TODOS.md updates** — 0 proposed. Every evidenced gap is repaired in scope. Candidates rejected as expansions under HOLD SCOPE: auto-recovery from BYPASSED, cap growth, prewarming. Step evaluated, not skipped.

### Diagrams

§1 System architecture
```
  caller ──▶ authn/authz ──▶ readProfile / writeProfile (wrapper)
                                │           │            │
                                ▼           ▼            ▼
                       flag.readsEnabledFor  LRU adapter   single-flight (+invalidate)
                                                │            │
                                                └──▶ repository.read/write ──▶ DB
  metrics/logs ◀── wrapper + adapter (D5)
```

§2a Data flow with shadow paths (read)
```
  key ──▶ flag? ──▶ cache.get ──▶ single-flight ──▶ repository.read ──▶ fill? ──▶ return
   │        │          │              │                  │               │
  nil/bad   lookup     undefined      join or start      null (absent)   invalidated → skip
  key:      fails:     = miss;        leader error →     → cache null    oversize → skip
  rejected  reads      null = ABSENT  joiners get it     DB error →      adapter throw →
  by exist- disabled   hit            no fill            typed error     BYPASSED
  ing valid.
```

§2b Async ordering schedule (invariant boundary: `writeProfile` returns)
```
  t   R1 (read)               W (write)                 R2 (read)         cache      result
  1   miss, start DB read v1                                              —
  2                           DB commits v2                               —
  3                           finally: delete,                            —
                              invalidate(R1 flight); returns
  4a  resume: invalidated →                                               —          R1 gets v1 (allowed)
      skip fill, return v1
  5a                                                    miss → fresh      v2         R2 gets v2 ✓
                                                        flight → v2, fill
  4b                                                    miss → NOT joined —
                                                        (flight detached)
      [without D1: 4a fills v1 → R2 hits v1 ✗ up to 30 s; 4b joins R1 → R2 gets v1 ✗]
  Alt order: R1 resumes at t2.5 before W's finally → fills v1 → t3 delete removes it ✓
```

§3 State machine (adapter state, per process)
```
  DISABLED ──flag on──▶ ACTIVE ──adapter throws──▶ BYPASSED
     ▲                    │                            │
     └────flag off────────┴─────────flag off───────────┘
  Invalid: BYPASSED → ACTIVE without passing DISABLED (prevented: only
  flag-off drops the instance; flag-on constructs a new empty one).
  Entry states: MISS → FILLED(v, 30 s) | ABSENT(10 s) → deleted by write / TTL / eviction.
```

§4 Error flow

```
  repository error ──▶ single-flight releases ──▶ no fill ──▶ typed API error (unchanged)
  adapter throw    ──▶ BYPASSED + log + gauge=2 ──▶ read continues to DB ──▶ alert at 5 min
  write error      ──▶ finally: delete + invalidate ──▶ rethrow typed error
```
